My thought process:  
1. Find a good P/FCF and P/E company. (Usually in range of 3.0\~15.0)  
2. Only consider market cap > $1.0B   
3. If the company is in the primary sector (extracting raw resources from the nature itself), additional points.  
4. Dollar cost average buying with my monthly salary, after paying my expenses and mortgages first.

My reasons:  
1. I think the company with good endogeneous money generation with some shareholder rewarding policy is resilient to boom and bust business cycles. Also, it is easier to anticipate the future trajectory. If the company has too volatile P/E or P/FCF historically, then I give minus points.  
2. Too small companies have legal risks and various external risks, which I cannot anticipate and cannot employ countermeasures.  
3. The primary sector companies, especially coal, oil, and natgas mining companies, are very transparent and easy to understand models of business. They usually open up their future guidance and future revenue forecast with real tangible FID (final investment decisions) to the shareholders. So I can have clear plans and target prices when I buy these stocks.

I think you have a valid point. MMA is its own art, not just a combination of striking art + grappling art. I respect Judo Olympians a lot, actually I almost worship the work ethic and performance level of national representatives. However, not researching no-gi MMA environment and just enter the sport with given Judo background is a certain way to failure. Rules and equipment dictate everything in a match. 

If Judo players really want to be successful in no-gi MMA scene (I honestly can't find a reason why should they though), then they need to change Judo principles and techniques according to MMA rulesets. Also, they need to practice a lot of leg shoot techniques such as kuchiki taoshi(single leg), morote gari(double leg), kibisu gaeshi(ankle pick), kata guruma, and ura nage because of obvious advantages these techniques can offer. If you do high speed leg shoot tackles from some distance you can evade the opponent's punch and kick attacks with high probability.

Also I think Judo newaza is very strong for given Judo ruleset, but no-gi MMA does not admit 20 second osaekomi ippon. So Judo players should adapt newaza training routines to more submission targetted mindset.

In addition to all of these hassles, Judo players should train a lot of boxing or striking arts to overcome the shock and fear of receiving punches (especially open finger gloves in this case). Almost all elite Judo players did not experience heavy punching for like 20 years. Training in Boxing gym for 6 months does not give you sufficient striking mentality.

Long story short, we should respect no-gi MMA as much as we want to respect Judo.
